To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) different nucleon-nuclon (NN) interaction cross sections have only minor effects on the fragment distribution in central collisions, (ii) the influence on the fragment distribution increases at semicentral collisions and (iii) it is strongly enhanced at peripheral collisions.

different nucleon-nuclear cross sections have small effect on fragment production at low energies, but at higher energies, different NN cross sections have small influences on fragment production for the central collisions, whereas fragment production is strongly dependent at the peripheral collisions.
the fragment production in the quantum molecular dynamics is not strongly dependent on the choice of the nucleon-nuclear cross section at low energies, but it is at higher energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how different NN cross sections influence the fragment production.
the influence of different cross sections on the multifragmentation process and on the fragment flow in heavy-ion collisions.
a systematic study of different nucleon-nucleron cross sections in the framework of a microscopic transport model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of the NN cross section does not change the fragment production at low energies, while the influence is significant at higher energies.
the choice of the NN cross section is important for the description of the fragment distribution at intermediate and high energies.
the fragment distribution is sensitive to the choice of the NN cross section at higher energies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the influence of the NN cross sections on the fragment production is reduced if the clusterization algorithm is used.

the fragment formation in heavy-ion collisions at low energies is mainly governed by the dynamics of the system, whereas at higher energies the fragment formation is more influenced by the nucleon-nuclear interaction.
the fragment production is not sensitive to the cross section for low-energy reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a constant NN cross section should not be used to describe the multifragment production at different bombarding energies.
the choice of the nucleon-nuclear cross section has a significant effect on fragment production at peripheral collisions and on the fragment distribution at high energies.
a constant energy-dependent cross section is sufficient for describing the multifragmentation process.
